item.title: Census Bureau Profile America Facts for Features: National Black History Month: February 2026
item.description: Historian Carter G. Woodson launched Black History Week in 1926 to recognize the significant contributions of African Americans during the second week of February to coincide with the birthdays of Abraham Lincoln (February 12) and abolitionist/writer Frederick Douglass (February 14). Congress expanded it to National Black History Month 50 years later during the nation’s bicentennial […]

item.title: Moore’s Ford Bridge: Remembering America’s Last Mass Lynching
item.description: It marks the site of the Moore's Ford Bridge lynching — widely recognized as the last documented mass lynching in the United States.
